learning_outcomes.text: Understand and identify the different mechanisms of heat transfer: conduction, convection, and radiation.
Know how to formulate and solve energy balances on a surface.
Understand and apply the General Conduction Equation, including the appropriate formulation of initial and boundary conditions.
Know and apply the concepts of thermal resistance and overall heat transfer coefficient.
Know how to design and quantify the efficiency of extended surfaces.
Understand the concept of transient heat conduction and know the resolution alternatives in such situations.
Know the limitations of analytical solutions and the formulation of numerical resolution methods.
Know the equations governing heat transfer by convection and the dimensionless treatment of such problems.
Apply analytical and experimental solutions in forced or natural convection situations.
Know the most common types of heat exchangers and their operation.
Know the methods of analysis for heat exchangers.
Know the electromagnetic radiation spectrum, identifying the thermal radiation band.
Correctly evaluate radiation balances between surfaces or on a surface located in open spaces.

assessment_rules: There are two alternative options to pass the course. Option 1 computes the final grade from an exam (70-80%), other evaluation activities (0-10%), and practical assignments (10-20%), requiring completion of at least 80% of practical sessions and submission of all mandatory practical deliverables. Failure to meet these commitments results in evaluation by Option 2. Option 2 consists of a final exam covering the entire syllabus, whose grade will be the final course grade. For Option 1, a minimum grade of 4 on the exam is required to average with other evaluations. The final exam will consist of 3-6 exercises, last 2-3 hours, and require numerical values and units, with a maximum score of 3/10 for physically nonsensical solutions.
